bakeoff.bias: The gates and the prompts of the pipeline were tuned on JEV, so JEV is read with that bias in its favour: Decisions is scored at the gate that was set for JEV. The best gate of each backend is chosen from a sweep on the same questions it is scored on, so it is in sample and flatters the backend. The questions come from the same distribution the gates were tuned on, not from a hold-out. The verify labels come from one LLM judge, and a task is led only when a paired sign test says so.

latency.caveat: The latency pass is one run of 30 triage asks per backend, not interleaved (JEV first, then Decisions), at one time of day; it covers triage asks only.
latency.what: wall time of one fresh decider ask, in seconds, on a temporary cache
